recognize_zh: 臨床照片：幼兒的手背與腕部明顯腫脹、皮膚緊繃發亮並泛紅，手指也略浮腫；鐮刀型貧血幼童出現這種手足對稱或單側的疼痛性腫脹，應想到小骨梗塞造成的指（趾）炎（hand-foot syndrome）。
features: Young child's hand and distal forearm photographed on a hospital drape
Diffuse swelling of the dorsum of the wrist and hand with tense, shiny skin
Focal erythema over the dorsal wrist region
Mild puffiness of the fingers; no ulceration, pustule or open wound visible
Small superficial abrasions/marks on the swollen skin (possibly cannulation or adhesive sites)
describe_en: Clinical photograph shows a young child's hand with diffuse, tense swelling of the dorsum of the wrist and hand, overlying shiny skin, and focal erythema, with mild puffiness of the fingers. There is no visible ulceration, abscess pointing, or necrosis. Clinical photographs cannot distinguish vaso-occlusive infarction from infection, so imaging, inflammatory markers, and blood cultures are needed. In a young child with sickle cell disease, the findings are consistent with dactylitis (hand-foot syndrome) due to vaso-occlusive infarction of the small bones.

ddx.vs: Osteomyelitis is favored by persistent high fever, progressive unilateral focal swelling, positive blood cultures and MRI findings of abscess, and it may coexist with infarction.
Cellulitis shows spreading warm erythema with a skin portal of entry and fluctuance on exam rather than primarily bony-origin symmetric swelling.
JIA causes joint-centered swelling lasting more than 6 weeks without the acute self-limited course of sickle dactylitis.
Extravasation swelling is localized to a recent IV site with a clear temporal relationship to infusion.
